pages.summary: Image files read and written, and what they hold.
body: PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF and GIF. `imread` gives uint8 values (uint16 for 16-bit images): m-by-n for grey, m-by-n-by-3 for colour, and for an image with a palette its indices (from 0) and colormap. `imwrite` takes the format from the file name; doubles are taken as 0 to 1, and `'Quality'` sets JPEG's compression. `imfinfo` gives the size, bit depth, colour type and format.

examples.title: A gradient written and read back

pages.summary: An image shown: a matrix of colour indices, or an m-by-n-by-3 array of colours.
body: A matrix is drawn through the figure's colormap, each value an index into it (doubles from 1, integers from 0); an m-by-n-by-3 array as colours (doubles 0 to 1, or uint8 0 to 255). Rows run down from the top. `x` and `y` place the image's corners; `imagesc` scales a matrix to the whole colormap instead.

examples.title: Each value a row of the colormap
examples.intro: Nine values, nine colours: 1 is the colormap's first row, 9 its last.
examples.code:
C = magic(3)
image(C), colormap(parula(9)), axis image

pages.summary: WAV files written, read, and described.
body: `audiowrite` writes samples (a column per channel, -1 to 1 for doubles) at a sample rate, in 16 bits unless `'BitsPerSample'` says; `audioread` gives the samples as doubles (or `'native'`) and the rate, or a range of samples; `audioinfo` the channels, rate, samples, duration and bits.

examples.title: A second of a tone in stereo

pages.summary: Data read from a web address, sent to one, and saved to a file; and the options for doing so.
body: `webread` reads JSON (as structs and arrays), text, an image or bytes, with query names and values added to the address; `webwrite` sends data (a form's name-value pairs, or a body) and reads the answer; `websave` saves what an address gives to a file. `weboptions` sets the timeout, content type, header fields, method, user name and password. In the page, only servers that allow other sites to read them (CORS) can be read. A `data:` address holds its data in itself, which the examples use.

examples.title: JSON and text from data addresses
examples.output:
d = 

  struct with fields:

      site: 'N'
    depths: [3×1 double]

ans =

    12    14    13


hello from the web

ans =

    10

pages.summary: Video files written frame by frame, and read back.
body: `VideoWriter` writes AVI files (Motion JPEG unless `'Uncompressed AVI'` or `'Grayscale AVI'`): set `FrameRate` and `Quality`, `open` it, `writeVideo` frames (from `getframe`, or images), and `close` it. `VideoReader` reads AVI files and animated GIFs: `NumFrames`, `FrameRate`, `Duration`, `Width` and `Height` describe them, `hasFrame` and `readFrame` go through the frames, and `CurrentTime` says where the next is read.

examples.title: Ten frames of a moving square, written and counted back

pages.summary: Frames of a video; the next block of a datastore.
body: For a `VideoReader`: all the frames, frame k, a range, or the last (`Inf`), stacked in the fourth dimension. For a datastore: its next `ReadSize` rows (or file, image, slice), with information about where they came from.

examples.title: Frames from a short video

pages.summary: A player of sound samples, and its controls.
body: `audioplayer(y, Fs)` holds the samples (a column per channel, -1 to 1 for floating point) and plays them through the page's sound: `play` starts and the program goes on, `playblocking` waits until the end, `pause` stops where it is and `resume` goes on, `stop` stops; `isplaying` says whether it plays now, and `CurrentSample` where it is.

examples.title: A player made and started
examples.intro: Run it in the page to hear it.

pages.summary: A recorder of the microphone, and its controls.
body: `audiorecorder(Fs, nBits, nChannels)` (8000 Hz, 8 bits, 1 channel unless given) records through the page, which the browser asks permission for: `record` starts and the program goes on (for a length, or until `stop`), `recordblocking` waits until it has recorded the length, `isrecording` says whether it records now, and `getaudiodata` gives what was recorded, a column per channel. Recording needs the page and a microphone, so the example writes a program to run there.

examples.title: A recorder, and a program that records two seconds
